featured_reviews.name: Rishabh Sinha
featured_reviews.review_text:
During a recent visit to Huckleberry’s The Cake Shop with my uncle and father, we found ourselves in a situation that prompted me to share my thoughts as a customer, despite the initial discomfort. I’d like to acknowledge the establishment’s rich history since 1953, a hidden gem that had eluded my awareness until then.

Accompanied by my senior-aged uncle and my father on a business visit, we entered the shop with the intention of exploring and appreciating the products offered. I extend my sincere apologies for any perceived imposition from my senior-aged uncle, especially in light of language differences.

Upon entering the shop, I was captivated by the variety of offerings, particularly the unique chocolates on display. However, my excitement waned when I sampled the chocolates, especially the pineapple and blueberry flavors. Regrettably, the taste was lackluster, and the cookies seemed to have lost their freshness, possibly due to extended storage.

Opting for a small chocolate cake with medium sugar levels, priced at 225 rupees, I was disappointed when the sweetness overwhelmed the cake’s original flavor. It felt more like consuming sugar than savoring a cake, leaving my taste buds wanting.

Interactions with the shop owner and staff were satisfactory, but there was a slight lapse in judgment regarding understanding customers’ preferences, especially when it comes to purchasing cakes for occasions. A more polite inquiry about preferences would greatly enhance the overall customer experience.

While I appreciate the loyalty of the established fanbase, I believe there’s an opportunity to broaden the brand’s appeal to a more diverse customer base. This is a subjective observation, and I understand that tastes can vary.

Moreover, I couldn’t help but notice an ambiance that struck me as somewhat unique and apocalyptic. Its distinctive atmosphere could serve as an interesting reference model for scriptwriters exploring unconventional settings.

In conclusion, I share these insights with humility and respect, hoping that they contribute positively to the continuous improvement of Huckleberry’s The Cake Shop. I believe constructive feedback is essential for growth, and I express these thoughts with the intention of contributing to the enhancement of the overall customer experience. Thank you for providing an opportunity to express my thoughts.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Emrik - The Cake Point💕
If you’re a dessert lover like me, this cozy little spot is a dream come true! The warm lighting, pastel aesthetics, and subtle aroma of fresh bakes make it a perfect hideout for a sweet indulgence session.

They’ve got lots of unique Rakshabandhan gifting options – from beautifully packed pastries and brownies to assorted hampers, chocolate bouquet, etc. Thoughtful, delicious, and way better than boring old gifts🎁💛

Here’s what we tried (and loved!):

Ferrero Rocher Pastry - Rich, creamy, and every bite melts in your mouth. It had the perfect hazelnut-chocolate balance – like eating a Ferrero in cake form!

Hazelnut Crunchy Pastry - This one was a textural delight! Soft cake layers meet crunchy hazelnut bits – just indulgent enough.

Puff - Flaky, buttery, and served warm – this one was simple yet so satisfying. Ideal if you’re not in the mood for something too sugary.

Nutella Brownie - Dense, gooey, and loaded with Nutella – this is not your regular brownie. It hits all the right notes for a chocoholic!

Rasmalai Dessert - A fusion done right! Creamy layers with that unmistakable rasmalai flavor – desi meets patisserie in the best way possible.

Nutella Donut - Soft, fresh donut filled with oozing Nutella – need I say more? Just heavenly.

Think Pinterest café vibes – perfect for a catch-up with friends or a solo coffee & cake moment. Bonus: Staff was super warm and welcoming too!

Definitely going back for round 2🫣

Extremely Disappointed — Ruined My Dad’s 60th Birthday!

I had placed a pre-scheduled order with Emrik Cake more than 6 hours in advance through Zomato for my dad’s 60th birthday celebration. The order was accepted by the shop, so I assumed everything was confirmed. But right at the time of delivery, I got a casual call from their staff saying “the cake is not in stock.” Seriously?
How can a bakery accept an order, sit on it for hours, and then inform the customer at the last minute — especially for such an important occasion?

Because of their complete lack of professionalism and responsibility, we had no cake for my dad’s milestone birthday. Totally unacceptable. If you care about reliability, timely service, or any special occasion, please avoid this place. They clearly have no value for customers or commitments.
